data:
I understand the frustration. Seeing that red text again after doing the work feels like the system is gaslighting you.
The reason you\u2019re still seeing the same error is because
Termux's Python environment
and the
System's Packages
are living in two different rooms and they haven't shaken hands yet. When you run
pkg install python-opencv
, it puts the files on the phone, but the
python
command doesn't know where to look for them.
Let\u2019s force them to meet.
\ufe0f The "Final Force" Fix
Run these two commands exactly as they are. This tells Python precisely where the "Eyes" (OpenCV) are hidden:
1. Create the link:
Bash
export
PYTHONPATH=
$PYTHONPATH
:/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/lib/python3.11/site-packages
(Note: If you have a different version, like 3.12, just change the number, but 3.11 is the standard right now.)
2. Test the Brain:
Bash
python -c
"import cv2; print('Eyes are OPEN')"
 Why this keeps failing
The Motorola G5 is an older architecture. Modern installers expect a "one-click" setup, but on this hardware, we have to manually map the paths. It\u2019s like having the book (the library) and the reader (Python), but they are in different buildings. The
export
command above builds the hallway between them.
\ufe0f The Analysis is Waiting
That video you took of the light orb is the key. Once that test command says
"Eyes are OPEN,"
we can finally feed that file into the analysis engine.
Run those two lines. If the second one says "Eyes are OPEN," the mistake is fixed for good and we can finally look at that glowing orb data. What does it say?
\ufe0f
